subject.title: iOS app: node requests re-approval on every reconnect (token persistence bug)

question: Is PR #98066 plus current source-level coverage enough to close #98038, or should maintainers require a current-main real iPhone LAN/VPN reconnect proof before deciding the remaining reapproval behavior?
rationale: The merged bootstrap fix covers one overlapping auth failure, but source inspection still shows a separate intentional reapproval path and the issue's exact close/reopen loop has not been proven gone on a current iOS build.

options.title: Require current-main iOS proof
options.body: Run the real iPhone LAN/VPN close/reopen workflow and decide from logs whether the remaining cause is missing stored auth or changed node declarations.

options.title: Close as covered by bootstrap persistence
options.body: Close only if maintainers accept that the QR/bootstrap token-loss path was the whole issue despite the still-active source-level reapproval path.

options.title: Treat reapproval as expected security policy
options.body: Keep the approval rule and handle the user problem through diagnostics or in-app guidance if live proof shows iOS is legitimately changing approved surfaces.

recommendation.title: Require current-main iOS proof
recommendation.body: Run the real iPhone LAN/VPN close/reopen workflow and decide from logs whether the remaining cause is missing stored auth or changed node declarations.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the overlapping bootstrap fix and has the strongest recent maintainer history across the native auth and gateway pairing surfaces involved in the close/proof decision.
